_comment_navigation: URLAllowlist takes precedence over URLBlocklist, so the two entries below
are the only pages the kiosk browser can reach at all. This is the layer
that keeps the manager on screen: even when a shortcut slips past Openbox,
Ctrl+J, Ctrl+H, Ctrl+U, F12 and view-source have nowhere to navigate to.
If loading.html ever moves, this allowlist entry has to move with it or the
kiosk will boot to a blocked page. The directory is allowed alongside the
exact URL purely as a hedge: nothing under /opt/penlive is secret, and the
cost of getting the file:// match wrong is a stick that boots to nothing.
_comment_startup: Any window Chromium opens on its own lands on the loading page, which forwards to the manager once the API answers — never on a blank tab.
_comment_shortcuts: Each of these turns one browser keyboard shortcut into a no-op: Ctrl+Shift+N, F12/Ctrl+Shift+I/J, Ctrl+J/Ctrl+S, Ctrl+P, Ctrl+O, Ctrl+Shift+M, Ctrl+D/Ctrl+Shift+O, Shift+Esc.
_comment_interstitials: An offline kiosk must never show a full-page Safe Browsing or search-engine interstitial: it reads as the manager having crashed.
